objects.name: Transformation Architecture (R1 / R2 / R3)
objects.equation: A mathematical structure may be investigated by distinguishing: (1) how it transforms when its representation changes, (2) which transformations leave the structure invariant, and (3) which maps/operators remain compatible with those transformations. R1 representation covariance; R2 structural invariance / symmetry (F*T = T); R3 equivariance / intertwining (C ρ_V(g) = ρ_W(g) C)
objects.failureCondition: vacuity: if every transformation could be sorted into some level, the architecture would organize nothing; each level must name its class, law, invariant and a failure (TRA2b, TRA3b, TRA4a, TRA4b)
objects.foundationRole: PROJECT-LEVEL ORGANIZING ARCHITECTURE, DERIVED FROM ESTABLISHED MATHEMATICS (not a new theorem); supersedes CF11-R; history: CF11 → Fisher test → CF11-F2 → architectural correction → R1/R2/R3

objects.name: R1 — Representation covariance

A change of description, not an active symmetry: never written F*g = g [Notation: here J = ∂θ/∂φ is the reparametrization Jacobian, written A in the model-manifold records (g_φ = Aᵀ g_θ A); the prediction Jacobian is J_Y = ∂Y/∂θ (MMPc).]
objects.failureCondition: a lossy map (projection) is not R1 (TRA4b); a coordinate-dependent pseudo-structure does not transform covariantly (CFT10a)
objects.foundationRole: formalizes one of the oldest project questions (H2): different representations may look different while preserving deeper structure

objects.name: R2 — Structural invariance / symmetry
objects.equation: active symmetry: F*T = T. objects.failureCondition: non-symmetries fail (CFT1c, CFT2b, CFT4d); preserving zeros does not imply invariance (TRA2b)
objects.foundationRole: Several major geometries in the Foundation admit a coordinate-free symmetry condition in which a defining tensor/form is preserved under pullback (established mathematics)

objects.name: R2, infinitesimal: L_X T = 0

objects.name: R3 — Equivariance / intertwining
objects.equation: C ρ_V(g) = ρ_W(g) C for a map C: V → W (intertwiner); when V = W with one representation, C ρ(g) = ρ(g) C (commuting operator). Examples: Fourier F T_a = M_a F (translation ↔ phase multiplication); weighted centering A C_m = C_m A for D-isometries preserving span{1}; Pₙ commutes with permutations; S² commutes with the S₄ action (Schur sectors)
objects.failureCondition: commuting or intertwining is not invariance: C_m is not an isometry, the DFT is not a symmetry of the shift (TRA3b)
objects.foundationRole: compatibility of derived maps / operators with transformations; not another form of structural invariance

reductionMaps.name: Simplex projection Pₙ: ℝⁿ → 1^⊥
reductionMaps.survives: pairwise differences vᵢ − vⱼ = eᵢ − eⱼ survive exactly while the common mode is removed; Σvᵢ = 0. The source Gram I does not survive: the projected simplex has the exact Gram matrix Pₙ = I − 11ᵀ/n (|vᵢ|² = (n − 1)/n, vᵢ·vⱼ = −1/n, G2n)
reductionMaps.zero: Pₙ1 = 0: a nonzero source with zero image; Pₙx = 0 ⟺ x ∈ span{1}
reductionMaps.reconstructible: under the orthonormal-source assumptions: the source as vᵢ + w, |w|² = 1/n, unique up to ±n̂ and an isometry (G3b, G3n); without the source class, no (G4c)

reductionMaps.name: Weighted centering C_m = I − 1mᵀ/M
reductionMaps.survives: relative positions: (C_m y)ᵢ − (C_m y)ⱼ = yᵢ − yⱼ
reductionMaps.collapses: y and y + c1 (the weighted common / translation mode)
reductionMaps.reconstructible: y from (C_m y, mᵀy/M); not from C_m y alone
reductionMaps.symmetry: commutes with D-isometries preserving span{1} (R3, CFT8c); not an isometry

reductionMaps.name: Fourier transform (unitary)
reductionMaps.symmetry: R1 (change of orthonormal basis) and R3 (F T_a = M_a F)

reductionMaps.name: Keeping Fourier magnitudes only (x ↦ |x̂|)
reductionMaps.survives: the power spectrum, equivalently the autocorrelation (second-order information)
reductionMaps.collapses: all translates; reversals of real signals; and signals unrelated by these (P1c)
reductionMaps.reconstructible: not in general (phase retrieval needs extra assumptions; none carded)
reductionMaps.fibers: signals with equal power spectrum (not a linear subspace)

reductionMaps.name: Discarding Fourier coefficients / band-limiting
reductionMaps.collapses: signals differing only in the discarded modes
reductionMaps.zero: P x = 0 ⟺ x lies in the discarded modes
reductionMaps.reconstructible: only for signals known to lie in the kept band

reductionMaps.name: Single wavelet / filter channel (x ↦ x ∗ ψ_λ)
reductionMaps.axisA: need not be invertible: injectivity depends on the signal space and the frequency response. Finite periodic / discrete: a zero-mean channel annihilates the constant mode (RIC2a). L²(ℝ): decided by the multiplier ψ̂_λ, not by zero mean alone; a zero set of measure zero gives injectivity (Mexican hat), possibly without a bounded inverse (RIC3a); a zero set of positive measure gives a nontrivial kernel (RIC3b). Information-changing whenever not injective, or not boundedly invertible
reductionMaps.survives: the part of x where ψ̂_λ is nonzero
reductionMaps.collapses: signals differing only where ψ̂_λ vanishes (finite periodic: the constant mode of a zero-mean channel; L²(ℝ): a nontrivial set only if that zero set has positive measure)
reductionMaps.zero: x with x̂ supported in the zero set of ψ̂_λ
reductionMaps.lost: content where ψ̂_λ vanishes; where ψ̂_λ is small, recoverable only without a bounded inverse
reductionMaps.reconstructible: not from one channel in general; an injective channel on L²(ℝ) may lack a bounded inverse (RIC3a)
reductionMaps.fibers: x + {y : ŷ supported in the zero set of ψ̂_λ}
reductionMaps.symmetry: translation covariance (T_a x) ∗ ψ_λ = T_a(x ∗ ψ_λ): an equivariance (R3) relation, not invariance

reductionMaps.name: Complete continuous wavelet transform (all required scales / translations)
reductionMaps.axisA: invertible on L²(ℝ) by the reconstruction formula, under the standard admissibility and finite-energy assumptions (Grossmann–Morlet; source-only); information-preserving under those assumptions. Different from the invertibility of one fixed channel
reductionMaps.lost: nothing under the assumptions; with restricted scales, the dropped bands
reductionMaps.reconstructible: yes: the reconstruction formula, under admissibility and finite energy (source-only)
reductionMaps.fibers: single points, under the stated assumptions

reductionMaps.name: Undecimated convolutional analysis bank x ↦ (H₁x, …, H_m x)
reductionMaps.axisA: injective iff, at every frequency of the stated signal space, some channel multiplier is nonzero (finite periodic: every DFT bin, carded RIC3c; L²(ℝ): almost every frequency, stated not carded); information-preserving when injective
reductionMaps.survives: everything, when the multipliers have no common zero on the signal space
reductionMaps.collapses: signals differing only at common zeros of all multipliers
reductionMaps.zero: x supported at the common zeros
reductionMaps.reconstructible: a left inverse exists in the finite periodic case when there is no common zero (RIC2a, RIC3c)
reductionMaps.fibers: x + {y supported at the common zeros}

reductionMaps.name: Critically sampled / multirate filter bank
reductionMaps.axisA: perfect reconstruction requires the analysis / synthesis polyphase system to be invertible, R(z)E(z) = c z^(−K) I (type-1 convention); the scalar no-common-zero condition is not sufficient (RIC3d: filters with no common zero, injective undecimated, give a non-invertible decimated bank); Haar satisfies R E = I
reductionMaps.survives: everything, when the polyphase system is invertible (Haar, RIC3d)
reductionMaps.collapses: when det E(z) vanishes on the unit circle: the corresponding polyphase component (RIC3d)
reductionMaps.reconstructible: iff the polyphase system is invertible; FIR perfect reconstruction iff R(z)E(z) = c z^(−K) I with FIR R
reductionMaps.fibers: x + ker of the decimated analysis map
reductionMaps.symmetry: covariant under shifts by the decimation factor only (not under all integer shifts)

reductionMaps.name: Wavelet modulus (|x ∗ ψ_λ|)
reductionMaps.survives: the envelope (local amplitude) in each band
reductionMaps.collapses: signals differing by phase within a band
reductionMaps.reconstructible: partly, through other bands and higher orders (source-only)

reductionMaps.name: Higher-order scattering propagation
reductionMaps.survives: part of what first-order averaging removes (source-only: Bruna–Mallat 2013)

reductionMaps.name: Finite-scale low-pass averaging (∗ φ_J)
reductionMaps.survives: content passed by φ_J (structure coarser than the averaging scale)
reductionMaps.collapses: signals differing only in what φ_J suppresses
reductionMaps.zero: components in the zeros of φ̂_J
reductionMaps.lost: detail finer than the averaging scale; high-frequency structure (higher orders retain part, source-only)
reductionMaps.symmetry: translation covariance (T_a x) ∗ φ_J = T_a(x ∗ φ_J) (RIC2b), NOT exact invariance; translation insensitivity / local invariance at the averaging scale is the sourced theorem (Mallat 2012), not carded

reductionMaps.name: Global average (full-domain sum, or the limit of infinite averaging scale)
reductionMaps.survives: the global average Σ|x ⊛ ψ| of the first-order modulus (FB10c)
reductionMaps.collapses: all translates; also x and its reversal (FB10c)
reductionMaps.symmetry: exact translation invariance under circular shifts for the full-domain sum (FB10c, RIC2b); in the continuous setting, invariance in the limit of infinite averaging scale (source-only, Mallat 2012); deformation stability (source-only)

reductionMaps.reconstructible: not from the dephased state alone
reductionMaps.fibers: states with the same block-diagonal part

reductionMaps.axisA: a degeneration of the model family (a limit), not a map Φ: X → Y on states; information-changing (in the F-C example the dimension drops 2 → 1; MMPl)
